From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ana Ruiz <ana@olivetech.com>
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan.park@olivetech.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request to reorder roadmap slot to unblock OliveTech close

Team —

Quick context: OliveTech (HS-OLV-4721) is at legal/PO stage and has made the roadmap request below a gating item for a May PO. They are proposing a $1.2M ARR commitment (3-year) if we can guarantee a limited-scope "tenant-level data residency and manual audit export hook" feature before deployment. Ana (Olivetech) is on the thread.

Why this matters: deal close by mid-May materially moves quarterly quota and opens a strategic reference in healthcare (their platform). If we miss May, they still intend to buy but timeline shifts to Q4 and momentum cools.

Ask: can Product/Eng consider swapping the current Q3 slot for a compact Q2 delivery (minimal viable scope) OR recommend a fall-back configuration that unlocks the deal without a full feature build? I want feasibility, rough timeline, and high-level risks by EOD tomorrow so I can set expectations with OliveTech.

Minimal scope proposal from Sales:
- A feature flag + config to opt a tenant into "data residency" (control routing to region X)
- An endpoint to export audit logs in a standardized CSV/JSON for customer auditors (manual export acceptable)
- Billing/entitlements changes optional (we can handle in billing later)

If full scope is needed we know the estimate will grow.

Attachments: OliveTech-MAP-v2.pdf (deal plan), Security-Questionnaire-OliveTech.pdf (they returned completed questionnaire)

Thanks — please mark owners and call out hard blockers.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher | Senior Account Exec, Strategic Deals | Redwood Inference

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ana Ruiz <ana@olivetech.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to reorder roadmap slot to unblock OliveTech close

Thanks for the signal, Sean. I read the MAP and questionnaire. High-level: product team is sympathetic but we need to be precise on scope to avoid a multi-quarter project. A minimal, safe path we can evaluate quickly:

Option A (fast):
- Config flag + routing policy that pins calls for a tenant to a particular region (no new infra, leverage routing layer)
- Export: one-off export API that dumps scoped audit logs (manual export, no UI)
Estimated: 2–3 weeks if we can allocate a small cross-functional squad and accept manual operational steps.

Option B (full):
- Full resident storage path + automated audit exports + UI controls + billing integration
Estimated: 8–10 weeks, higher QA and compliance review.

Tradeoffs and risks:
- Option A leaves us with operational overhead and potential edge cases for fallback routing.
- We will need security sign-off for Option A to ensure exports meet OliveTech's controls; the questionnaire has some unanswered items.
- We need a clear canary plan: how many requests/tenants to route before wider rollout.

Next steps I need from Sales by EOD tomorrow: a one-page must-have vs nice-to-have list (single bullet list), expected QPS/peak per minute, and confirmation OliveTech accepts manual export for first release. If they do, I can greenlight a 3-week timebox for a small squad to deliver Option A.

—Maya
Maya Srinivasan | Group PM, Platform Services | Redwood Inference

Quick engineering readout from infra/serving:

We can deliver a pragmatic Option A but with caveats. Rough breakdown:
- Spike (1 week): evaluate routing layer, confirm no cross-tenant KV leakage, prototype flag-based routing.
- Deliverable (3 weeks additional): flag + routed requests to region X, manual export endpoint for audit logs, basic acceptance tests.
Total: ~4 weeks but we can compress to ~3 if we pull staff from a lower-priority sprint.

Key dependencies:
- Ops: ephemeral capacity in region X for canary/testing.
- Security: export format must meet their compliance (PII redaction rules).
- Observability: need per-tenant traceid propagation and cost telemetry for the canary.

Fallback alternative (faster, 10 business days): use existing model-variant pinning + routing policy at the proxy layer; this avoids storage changes and gives the buyer the perceived residency (requests served in region X) but actual storage residency is not guaranteed — acceptable only if OliveTech signs an explicit acceptance and legal caveat.

If Sales confirms expected QPS and accepts manual export, we can begin a spike next week. Who will own the acceptance criteria and test vectors from OliveTech? Provide contact and sample queries.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick takes — actionable replies below.

1) OliveTech confirmation: Ana called earlier and confirmed they are ok with a manual export for first release provided we give a signed target date and a canary plan. She asked for a delivery target: end of May would be ideal (they want to run an audit in June).

2) QPS: Their platform peak for initial rollout is ~50 QPS with bursts to 120 QPS.

3) Acceptance ownership: Jordan Park (cc'd) will own acceptance testing on the OliveTech side and can provide sample queries and dataset snippets.

Given the engineering caveats, I propose we do Option A with the spike next week and a 3-week delivery window. If Product wants more runway, tell me the minimum gating items we must promise to OliveTech to get a PO before May 15.
